_README: Phase 0.6 Task 3. Every site in src/core/*.js that returns success:true, with a reason it is defensible. The rule: A TOOL MAY REPORT SUCCESS ONLY IF IT HAS OBSERVED THE STATE CHANGE IT CLAIMS TO HAVE CAUSED. tests/silent-success.test.js fails if a site appears here without a reason, or appears in the code without an entry here. Adding an entry is deliberately more effort than adding a read-back.

_classifications.read: Reports data it read. The returned data IS the evidence; it claims no state change.
_classifications.verified: Reached only after the claimed change was read back and compared.
_classifications.aggregate: A batch whose per-item verdicts carry the real answer.
_classifications.page-internal: A resolve() inside page-context JS, not a tool's return value.
_classifications.honest-partial: Reports what it did and explicitly disclaims readiness in the same payload.
_classifications.unobservable: A mutation whose effect this process cannot read back on this path; it returns unobservable(why), so the payload carries observed:false and names why instead of implying the effect happened.

alerts.js::create.why: Only returned when the alert service answers s==='ok'; the server-assigned alert_id is the evidence.

alerts.js::deleteAlerts.why: Only returned when the delete endpoint answers s==='ok'; the server is the observer here.

alerts.js::list.why: Returns the alert list fetched from TradingView's alert service; the alerts array is the evidence and no state is changed.

autopsy.js::compareAsFound.why: Compares the as-found record with a fresh read of the chart field by field; a field is answered only when the re-read value matches, otherwise failed(not_as_found).

autopsy.js::lossAutopsy.why: The packet carries per-view centring verdicts and the as-found restoration comparison; a thrown run returns failed(internal), so the inner verdicts are the answer.

backtest.js::backtestRun.why: Returns the strategy report read off the chart after a gated settle; the metrics are the evidence.

backtest.js::runDeepWindow.why: Returns the strategy report read after the gated settle for the requested window and fails with window_mismatch when the report does not describe it; reader failures are adopted failing.

backtest.js::walkForward.why: Returns per-window reports it read; each window carries its own numbers as evidence.

batch.js::batchRun.why: The outer flag means the sweep ran; each iteration carries its own success/error, and successful/failed counts are reported alongside.

capture.js::captureScreenshot.why: The CDP path writes the PNG to disk and returns its path; the file is the evidence. The 'api' path cannot observe its own effect and now returns unobservable() instead.

chart.js::(module).why: The applied() helper: returns success with settled:false and a fence, explicitly declining to claim the chart has caught up. Reads gate themselves at the read.

chart.js::getState.why: Returns the chart's symbol, resolution and study list as read; claims no change.

chart.js::getVisibleRange.why: Returns the visible range as read from the time scale.

chart.js::scrollToDate.why: The visible range is re-read and compared (observed/refused); unobservable() only when the range could not be read back, and the payload says so.

chart.js::setType.why: Observed/refused when the chart type can be read back; unobservable() only on a build exposing no readable chart-type accessor, and the payload says so.

chart.js::symbolInfo.why: Returns the chart's symbolExt() record as read - description, type, session, pricescale; it changes nothing.

chart.js::symbolSearch.why: Returns search results from TradingView's symbol search.

data.js::(module).why: gateRead with wait=false returns the current reading marked settled:false; it reports data it read and claims no change.

data.js::getDepth.why: Returns order-book depth rows as read; the bid/ask ladder is the evidence and nothing is submitted.

data.js::getEquity.why: Returns per-closed-trade equity read off the gated report; an empty book is failed(not_found), not a success.

data.js::getIndicator.why: Returns indicator series values read from the study.

data.js::getOhlcv.why: Returns bars read from the main series; the bars are the evidence.

data.js::getPineBoxes.why: Returns box objects read from a Pine study's drawing collection.

data.js::getPineLabels.why: Returns label objects read from a Pine study's drawing collection.

data.js::getPineLines.why: Returns line objects read from a Pine study's drawing collection.

data.js::getPineTables.why: Returns table objects read from a Pine study's drawing collection.

data.js::getQuote.why: Returns a real-time quote snapshot as read from the symbol's quote session; the prices are the evidence.

data.js::getStrategyResults.why: Returns the strategy metrics read off the gated report; an empty report is failed(not_found), not a success.

data.js::getStudyValues.why: Returns the current numeric values of visible indicators as read from their series; no inputs are written.

data.js::getTrades.why: Returns the trade list read off the gated report; an empty book is failed(not_found), not a success.

drawing.js::getProperties.why: Returns one shape's points and properties as read; throws when the shape is absent.

drawing.js::listDrawings.why: Returns getAllShapes() as read - one id and name per drawing; it claims no creation or removal.

equity.js::(module).why: readAllBars returns the price bars it read after extending history, and fails when the history never covered the requested span.

equity.js::equityCurve.why: Returns a curve reconstructed from the trade book and bars it read, with its own agreement check against the report; reader failures are adopted failing.

health.js::discover.why: Returns the probed TradingView API surface as read - which known paths resolve on this build; no state changes.

health.js::healthCheck.why: Returns the probed CDP and chart state; the probe results are the evidence.

health.js::uiState.why: Returns the observed UI state as read - which panels and dialogs are open; it opens nothing.

indicators.js::searchStudies.why: Success is computed as added.length > 0 from a before/after study-id diff, not asserted; the added ids are the evidence.

pane.js::focus.why: This build exposes no readable active-pane index, so where focus cannot be confirmed it returns unobservable() naming that, never a bare success.

pane.js::list.why: Returns the pane inventory as read from the chart widget collection - index, symbol and resolution per pane.

pane.js::setSymbol.why: The pane symbol is re-read and compared (observed/refused); unobservable() only when that pane symbol could not be read back.

pine-console.js::pineConsoleRead.why: Returns Pine log rows read from the study; a page result carrying no verdict becomes failed(internal) and failing page objects are adopted failing.

pine-inputs.js::(module).why: pageFailure() adopts a failing page-context object into a failed verdict, or failed(no_result); it is reached only on failure paths and cannot yield a success.

pine-inputs.js::pineInputsAssert.why: Answers only when every pinned input read back from the chart equals the manifest and the script identity matches; drift and mismatch are failed verdicts carrying the diff.

pine-inputs.js::pineInputsSnapshot.why: Returns the input values read via getInputValues() and their hash; it writes nothing to the chart.

pine-inputs.js::resolveEntity.why: Returns the one study resolved from the chart, refusing with ambiguous or not_found rather than choosing; the resolved id is the evidence.

pine.js::analyze.why: Returns static analysis of source text; touches no chart state.

pine.js::check.why: Returns the compile server's own verdict on submitted source; the server response is the evidence.

pine.js::compile.why: The compile button is clicked and the compilation result is not read back here; pine_get_errors and pine_smart_compile are the observing paths.

pine.js::getConsole.why: Returns the Pine console's output lines as read; it neither compiles nor clears the console.

pine.js::getErrors.why: Returns Monaco's current error markers as read - line, column, message, severity per marker.

pine.js::getSource.why: Returns the Pine editor's Monaco buffer contents as read; the source text is the evidence and nothing is written.

pine.js::listScripts.why: Returns the saved-script list fetched from pine-facade; the array of script names and ids is the evidence.

pine.js::newScript.why: The editor contents are compared with the template (observed/refused); unobservable() only when the buffer could not be read back after setValue().

pine.js::openScript.why: Reached only after the fetched source was injected into Monaco inside the page; line count and script id are the evidence.

pine.js::save.why: Ctrl+S is dispatched to the editor; whether TradingView accepted the save is not read back from this call, and the payload says so.

pine.js::setSource.why: The editor line count is read back (observed/refused); unobservable() only when the editor buffer could not be read back after setValue().

pine.js::smartCompile.why: Study addition is observed from the study-count delta; unobservable() only when the chart study count could not be read, so reaching the chart is unknown.

preflight.js::(module).why: loadManifest returns the manifest parsed from disk, or failed(reason) when it is not one; nothing on the chart is changed.

preflight.js::preflight.why: Returns every individual check with its own verdict and lists the failed ones; the overall answer derives from those checks and a bad manifest is adopted failing.

replay-manifest.js::assertStrategyManife.why: Answers only after the environment invariants and the manifest input comparison both pass; any mismatch throws ManifestMismatchError carrying the diff.

replay.js::health.why: Reports a classification of the replay session's state; the reading it classified is returned whole as `state`, and the optional step probe is returned as `probe`, so the verdict can be checked against its own evidence. Success means the health check ran - a wedged session is reported as wedged:true with success:true, because failing to return would withhold the one answer this call exists to give.

replay.js::status.why: Returns replay state as read: started flag, cursor, autoplay delay, position.

replay.js::stepUntil.why: Answered only when no bar was advanced (already_true, or stopped before the first step) with bars_advanced:0 saying so; any movement is observed with the before/after cursor.

tab.js::list.why: Returns the CDP page-target list as read, annotated with each target's chart id; it opens and closes nothing.

ui.js::click.why: The element is found and clicked; the effect of the click is not read back, and the payload says so.

ui.js::findElement.why: Returns matching DOM elements as read; claims no interaction.

ui.js::fullscreen.why: The fullscreen button is found and clicked; the resulting window state is not read back, and the payload says so.

ui.js::hover.why: The pointer is moved onto the located element; whether a hover state or tooltip resulted is not readable from here.

ui.js::keyboard.why: The key event is dispatched to the page; what the page did with it is not visible from here, and the payload says so.

ui.js::layoutList.why: Returns saved layouts from getSavedCharts; carries its own error field when the call times out.

ui.js::layoutSwitch.why: Both sites are resolve() calls inside the page-context promise, feeding the Node-side check. The tool's own return is built by the verdict helpers after polling layoutId().

ui.js::mouseClick.why: The click is dispatched at coordinates; what sits there and how it responded is not visible from here.

ui.js::openPanel.why: Open state is re-read and compared (observed/refused); unobservable() only when the panel container could not be read back after the click.

ui.js::scroll.why: The wheel event is dispatched; the resulting scroll position is not read, and the chart may have consumed it as a zoom.

ui.js::typeText.why: Text is inserted into whatever holds focus; this call does not know what that was or whether it accepted the text.

ui.js::uiEvaluate.why: Returns the evaluated expression's result, awaiting promises so a rejection throws rather than serialising as {}.

update.js::update.why: Returns git rev-parse output taken after the fast-forward; the before/after commit hashes are the evidence.

watchlist.js::get.why: Returns the watchlist rows as read from the right-hand panel; it adds and removes nothing.
